## Studio Albums

| Album | Year | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| *Busyhead* | 2019 | Debut studio album; leaned toward pop production. |
| *I Was / I Am* | 2021 | Second album, marking an early shift in sound. |
| *Stick Season* | 2022 | Breakout folk-pop album; his commercial peak. |
| *Stick Season (We'll All Be Here Forever)* | 2023 | Deluxe reissue with additional tracks and features. |
| *Stick Season (Forever)* | 2023 | Further expanded edition closing out the era. |

: {.album-table}

## EPs

- **Cape Elizabeth** (2021) — A stripped-back, folk-leaning EP that foreshadowed the *Stick Season* sound.

## Notable Songs

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### "Stick Season"
The title track and signature hit — a wistful account of heartbreak and homesickness set against the
Vermont autumn.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### "Dial Drunk"
A frenetic, radio-friendly single about a late-night drunk call to an ex; later reworked as a duet with
Post Malone.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### "Northern Attitude"
A collaboration with Zach Bryan reflecting on the guardedness bred by a cold-weather upbringing.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### "You're Gonna Go Far"
An anthemic, string-laden track about watching someone you love outgrow their hometown.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### "Call Your Mom"
A tender duet with Lizzy McAlpine about checking in on the people you love during hard times.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### "Homesick"
An earlier fan favorite that captures the pull between wanting to leave a small town and never wanting to
leave it.
:::

:::
